issues.legal_issue: A substantial delay in completing a land acquisition does not invalidate the acquisition when the awards are made within the statutory time limit and the delay is not shown to result from deliberate bad faith or a colourable exercise of power.
material_facts: The acquisition covered land in 86 villages for a large planned township, and the project followed consideration of reports by expert committees.
The authorities received and considered more than 25,000 objections and had to plan and acquire a very large area.

Although the proceedings took a long time and the Court considered that they could have been completed earlier, it found no firm basis to conclude that the delay was deliberate or that the acquisition was initiated solely to suppress land prices.
The awards were made within the time allowed by the applicable statutory framework.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition proceedings were not invalidated by the delay because they were completed within the statutory time frame and were not shown to have been initiated or prolonged through deliberate bad faith or a colourable exercise of power.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 11A of the Land Acquisition Act, including its proviso, and relied on Kaliyappan v. State of Kerala and Gujarat State Corporation v. Valji Mulji Soneji for the principle that, where the statute prescribes the time within which an award may be made, acquisition completed within that time is not to be set aside merely for delay. Public authorities must act reasonably and fairly, and a colourable or mala fide exercise of power may invalidate an acquisition; Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi was also considered in assessing delay and planning context.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and substantial_delay and award_within_statutory_period and large_scale_planned_project and not deliberate_bad_faith

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a compulsory land acquisition.
predicates.substantial_delay: The acquiring authority took a substantial time to complete the acquisition proceedings.
predicates.award_within_statutory_period: The acquiring authority made the award within the applicable statutory time limit.
predicates.large_scale_planned_project: The acquisition formed part of a large project that had been planned for a public purpose.
predicates.deliberate_bad_faith: The acquiring authority deliberately delayed or used the acquisition power in bad faith or for a colourable purpose.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition challenge concerns a substantially delayed but timely completed acquisition for a large planned project, and deliberate bad faith is absent, the acquisition is not invalidated for delay.

issues.legal_issue: Acquisition for a planned township is not premature or a colourable attempt to peg land prices when genuine planning and a definite development purpose preceded the acquisition notices.
material_facts: Expert committees had examined the need to address congestion and urban growth and recommended metropolitan planning and development of new centres.
The State accepted the planning recommendations, established a regional planning framework, and formed a development corporation to establish the new township.

The Court found that issuing acquisition notices also served to discourage speculation and keep the project economically viable, but found no firm basis for concluding that price pegging was the sole purpose.
The relevant planning work and decision to establish the township preceded the acquisition notices, although the detailed plan was developed later.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was not shown to be a colourable exercise of power or premature for want of a genuine plan and development purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the public-purpose framework under Section 125 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, which treats land required for a new town as needed for a public purpose. It relied on the planning history and considered Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi, including the principle that acquisition may precede development and that a challenge based on the absence of a completed plan must be assessed in context.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and expert_planning_preceded_notices and definite_public_development_purpose and not sole_price_suppression_purpose

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a compulsory land acquisition.
predicates.expert_planning_preceded_notices: Expert bodies examined the development need and made planning recommendations before the acquisition notices were issued.
predicates.definite_public_development_purpose: The acquiring authority had decided to acquire land for a genuine public development project.
predicates.sole_price_suppression_purpose: The acquisition was initiated solely to hold down land prices for a possible future project, without a genuine present development purpose.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge concerns land supported by prior expert planning and a definite public development purpose, and price suppression was not its sole purpose, the acquisition is not treated as colorable or premature.

issues.legal_issue: A claim that acquired land comprised areas protected by a government exclusion policy cannot be resolved in the proceeding when the existence of those areas is a disputed question of fact.
material_facts: The government had a policy of excluding recorded village settlements, contiguous houses, and certain hamlets from acquisition.
The parties disputed whether the particular acquired lands contained areas covered by that policy.
The Court found that the disputed factual existence of those areas could not be determined in the proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to decide the exclusion claim because it depended on disputed facts about the existence of the protected areas.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the existence and location of the alleged settlements and hamlets as a disputed factual issue that could not be resolved in these proceedings; it also noted that the High Court had not accepted the claim.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a compulsory land acquisition.
predicates.exemption_claim_depends_on_disputed_site: The claimed exclusion from acquisition depends on whether particular protected settlements or hamlets existed on the acquired land, and the parties dispute that fact.

issues.definition: When an exclusion claim in a land acquisition challenge depends on disputed facts about the site, the court declines to determine that claim in the proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: Affected landowners entitled to alternative sites under a development scheme must be offered those sites at no more than the actual acquisition and development costs where delayed acquisition has made the compensation amount insignificant and ordinary site prices would make the offer illusory.
material_facts: The government had a scheme for offering alternative sites to persons whose land was compulsorily acquired.
The acquisition proceedings had remained pending for years, leaving compensation based on the earlier notice period insignificant.
The authorities were developing the acquired land and would incur acquisition and infrastructure development costs.
The landowners challenged the much higher prices proposed for alternative sites, and the Court found that ordinary prices could make the offer practically unavailable to them.
issues.conclusion: The concerned authorities were directed to offer the alternative sites under the scheme at the actual cost of acquisition and development, and no more.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the scheme for affected landowners and on State of U.P. v. Smt. Pista Devi. Although Section 21(2) of the Delhi Development Act did not apply to the acquisition before the Court, the Court treated its principle as wholesome and applicable to development authorities acquiring large tracts for urban land development.

predicates.urban_land_acquisition_case: The proceeding concerns acquisition of land for development in an urban area.
predicates.affected_owners_entitled_to_alternative_: The acquiring authority has a scheme under which affected landowners are entitled to alternative sites.
predicates.compensation_rendered_insignificant_by_d: The acquisition delay left the compensation amount based on an earlier valuation period insignificant to the affected landowners.
predicates.ordinary_site_price_makes_offer_illusory: The ordinary price charged for an alternative site would make the promised allotment practically unavailable to the affected landowners.

issues.definition: When affected owners in an urban land acquisition are entitled to alternative sites, delay has made their compensation insignificant, and ordinary site prices would defeat the offer, the sites must be offered at actual acquisition and development cost only.

issues.legal_issue: Dismissal of earlier petitions does not prevent their petitioners from receiving directions expressly extended to them in a later common judgment.
material_facts: Earlier special leave petitions and a review petition concerning the same acquisition had been dismissed.
The Court made directions in the present common judgment and expressly extended them to petitioners in the previously dismissed matters.
issues.conclusion: The petitioners in the previously dismissed petitions and review petition were entitled to the directions in the judgment despite those dismissals.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly extended its operative directions to the petitioners whose earlier special leave petitions and review petition had been dismissed.

predicates.common_acquisition_appeals: The proceeding is a group of related appeals concerning the same acquisition and disposed of by a common judgment.
predicates.prior_petitions_dismissed: Petitions concerning the same acquisition had been dismissed before the current judgment.
predicates.current_judgment_expressly_extends_direc: The current judgment expressly applies its directions to petitioners whose earlier petitions had been dismissed.

issues.definition: When a common judgment expressly extends its directions to petitioners whose earlier petitions were dismissed, those petitioners receive the extended directions.
